primary_findings.finding: Detroit had the worse raw point differential
primary_findings.interpretation: Detroit was outscored by 73 more points across the season.

primary_findings.finding: Detroit's defense allowed more points and yards per play
primary_findings.evidence: Detroit allowed 517 points and 6.4 opponent yards/play; Cleveland allowed 410 and 5.1
primary_findings.interpretation: The strongest aggregate distinction is Detroit's defensive performance.

primary_findings.finding: Cleveland's offense had more volume but more ball-security problems
primary_findings.evidence: Cleveland gained 4,942 yards and committed 41 turnovers; Detroit gained 4,292 yards and committed 29
primary_findings.interpretation: Cleveland generated more total yards but gave the ball away 12 more times.

primary_findings.finding: Cleveland scored fewer points and had worse drive efficiency
primary_findings.evidence: Cleveland 234 points and 22.0% drive scoring; Detroit 268 and 26.2%
primary_findings.interpretation: More yardage did not translate to better scoring output.

primary_findings.finding: Both went 0-16, but not in the same way
primary_findings.interpretation: The answer to 'which was worse' depends on whether the priority is overall margin/defense or turnovers/offensive conversion.
